PASSAGE VI
Make Our Blocks Super
Living in a city can come with excitement
and opportunity—and with noise pollution,
feelings of isolation, and little access to green space.
Some people are able to overlook these drawbacks.
To alleviate them, US officials should look to a novel
concept being implemented in Barcelona, Spain.
In the early 2000s, this densely populated city
began piloting the superblock: an area of three blocks by
three blocks in which most automobile traffic is prohibited,
from interior streets. The concept, proposed by urbanist
Salvador Rueda, allows those streets to become
“pedestrian first,” prioritizing access for walkers and
cyclists. Ideally, superblocks also include amenities
that encourage residents to congregate outside,
such as benches, green space, and playgrounds.
Eventually, city planners hope to install over
five hundred superblocks throughout Barcelona.
Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically
acceptable?
A. No Change
B.
with: excitement and opportunity,
C.
with, excitement and opportunity:
D.
with excitement and opportunity;
Which of the following choices most effectively leads
the reader from the previous sentence to the argument
that follows in the rest of the essay?
F. No Change
G.
But urban living doesn’t have to be defined by
these drawbacks.
H.
These are just some of the drawbacks of urban
living, however.
J.
And individual cities have their own unique
drawbacks.
Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically
acceptable?
A. No Change
B.
blocks, in which most automobile traffic, is
prohibited
C.
blocks, in which most automobile traffic is
prohibited,
D.
blocks in which most automobile traffic is
prohibited
Given that all the choices are accurate, which one
provides the most relevant support for the writer’s
main argument?
F. No Change
G.
An analysis by the Barcelona Public Health
Agency showed that by reducing local traffic and
inviting people to spend time outside, superblocks
have led to quieter, more social neighborhoods.
H.
While World Health Organization standards say
that cities should contain a minimum of 10 square
meters of green space per person, Barcelona
contains only 6.6 square meters per person.
J.
A study published in
Nature Sustainability
concluded that the layouts of Tokyo, Cairo, and
Mexico City are also well suited for superblocks.
